statement: For q>=2, let omega be a primitive qth root of unity and c a complex number with c^q=-1. On C^q set U e_k=omega^k e_k and V e_k=c e_(k-1 mod q). Then det(zI-U-V)=z^q and (U+V)^q=0.
assumptions: omega is a primitive qth root

statement: Fix an irrational theta and reduced rationals p_j/q_j tending to theta with q_j tending to infinity. The clock/shift pairs U_j,V_j from the nilpotent construction, with omega_j=exp(2*pi*i*p_j/q_j) and c_j=exp(pi*i/q_j), converge in all star-moments and in the norms of every fixed matrix-valued star-polynomial to the canonical irrational rotation pair u,v. This uses simplicity and the faithful canonical trace of the irrational rotation C*-algebra. The cached Fang--Jiang--Lin--Xu paper, arXiv:1210.4771v1, Theorem 12.2, identifies the Brown measure of u+v in this canonical tracial representation as Haar measure on the unit circle. Every finite sum U_j+V_j has empirical eigenvalue measure delta_0. This gives a candidate counterexample to the implication from arbitrary strong convergence to Brown-measure convergence, pending independent review and with no novelty claim. It does not address independent Ginibre ensembles or a free limiting family.
assumptions: simplicity of the irrational rotation C*-algebra

statement: Let (eta_x) be a real, stationary, square-integrable field on Z^d, d>=1, with covariance c(z)=Cov(eta_0,eta_z). Suppose sum_z |c(z)|<infinity, sum_z c(z)=0, and M_alpha=sum_z ||z||_infinity^alpha |c(z)|<infinity for some 0<alpha<=1. For every integer L>=1, Var(sum_(x in {1,...,L}^d) eta_x) <= d M_alpha L^(d-alpha). These assumptions on the infinite-volume covariance are sufficient for a power saving; they are not established here for ARW wake states.

statement: Let B be a bounded Jordan measurable set in R^2 of positive area. Let P_i be countably many disjoint open Jordan measurable patches covering B up to a null set. For every i fix a finite-period Z^2 pattern h_i and let f_i(j) be its fraction of height j in one period. Suppose a discrete configuration s_N on B intersect N^(-1)Z^2 differs from h_i(Nx) at o(N^2) sites in each fixed P_i intersect B. Then for every integer j its height-j frequency in B converges to (1/area(B)) sum_i area(B intersect P_i) f_i(j). This is a sufficient condition; the required patchwise agreement for the actual sandpile, and the sandpile identity-element limit, are not proved here.
assumptions: B bounded Jordan measurable with positive area
patches cover B up to a null set
fixed finite-period pattern in each patch
o(N^2) mismatches in each fixed patch

statement: Weak-* convergence of bounded lattice height functions to a constant does not by itself imply convergence of each height frequency. Alternating arrays equal to 1 everywhere, or to a fine checkerboard of heights 0 and 2, both converge weak-* to 1, while the height-1 frequencies are respectively 1 and 0. A sequence alternating these two array types has a weak-* limit and no height-1 frequency limit. These are generic bounded arrays, not claimed to be stabilized sandpiles.

statement: Let tau_i be independent standard Brownian first hitting times of -1. For a deterministic exceptional-index set let m(N) count its first N indices and S_N=sum_(i=1 to m(N)) tau_i. For m(N)>0 and epsilon>0, P(S_N>epsilon N)=erf(m(N)/sqrt(2 epsilon N)). Thus S_N/N tends to zero in probability if and only if m(N)/sqrt(N) tends to zero. A zero density m(N)/N->0 alone is insufficient. If m(N)=O(N^(1/2-delta)) for some delta>0, then S_N/N->0 almost surely. These are clock statements, not a construction of a backward or two-sided Brownian law after a finite random shift.
assumptions: m(N) counts the first N indices

statement: For finite irreducible reversible chains, any universal K satisfying t_stop(P_hat)<=K t_stop(P) for every stationary-flow lumping must obey K>=3/2. Here t_stop(P)=max_i inf_T E_i T for randomized stopping times with terminal law pi. A four-state family with symmetric weights W=[[0,0,1,0],[0,2s,1,2s],[1,1,0,s],[0,2s,s,4s^2]], P_ij=W_ij/sum_k W_ik, s>0, and blocks {0},{1},{2,3}, has t_stop(P)->2 and t_stop(P_hat)->3 as s->infinity. This proves a candidate lower bound only; existence or sharpness of a universal K is not settled here. Independent review is pending.
assumptions: stationary-flow lumping, not a Markov projection
standard optimal stationary-stopping identity t_stop=max_(i,j)(H_ij-E_pi H_.j)

statement: In the normalized second Ray-Knight identity on a finite symmetric network pinned at a base vertex, the field identity in law is {L_(tau(t))^x + phi_x^2/2}_x =_d {(phi_x+sqrt(2t))^2/2}_x, with the left Gaussian field independent of the walk. It does not assert L_(tau(t))^x =_d (phi_x+sqrt(2t))^2/2. When Var(phi_x)=g>0 and t>0, the local-time marginal has mean t and an atom exp(-t/g) at zero, whereas the shifted Gaussian square has mean t+g/2 and no atom at zero. The omitted term in the earlier C0011 attempt invalidates that transfer step. This correction does not decide present openness of the full planar level-set problem.
assumptions: finite symmetric network with normalized pinned Ray-Knight identity
Gaussian field on the left independent of the walk

statement: Let L have Laplace transform E exp(-lambda L)=exp(-t lambda/(1+g lambda)), lambda>=0, where t>0 and g>0. For ell>=t, P(L>=ell)<=exp(-(sqrt(ell)-sqrt(t))^2/g). For 0<=ell<=t, P(L<=ell)<=exp(-(sqrt(ell)-sqrt(t))^2/g). At ell=0 the bound is exact: P(L=0)=exp(-t/g). This supplies a one-point rate, not joint spatial convergence of a local-time level set.

statement: Let a Poisson(lambda) Galton-Watson process have lambda>1 and extinction probability q in (0,1), satisfying q=exp(-lambda(1-q)). Conditional on extinction its offspring law is Poisson(lambda q). If I(a)=a-1-log a, then I(lambda q)=I(lambda) exactly. For lambda=1+epsilon with epsilon decreasing to zero, lambda q=1-epsilon+(2/3)epsilon^2+O(epsilon^3). This is a branching-process mechanism for discrete duality; it does not prove that hypercube clusters after deleting the giant have this law.
assumptions: q is the nontrivial extinction root

statement: Let tau be uniform on [T,2T], T>0, and let A and B be products of at most r prime factors each, all primes <=y, y>=2. For A=B, E exp(-i tau log(A/B))=1. For A!=B its modulus is at most min(1,2/(T |log(A/B)|))<=min(1,2 y^r/T). Independent Haar phases at the primes have the same expectation 1 when A=B and 0 otherwise. Thus for a finite polynomial in these phases and their conjugates with such monomials and coefficient absolute sum M, the time-average versus Haar moment error is at most 2 M y^r/T. This is a sufficient fixed-moment approximation window, not a necessary condition and not a decomposition theorem for log|zeta|.
assumptions: each prime product has at most r factors <=y
finite polynomial with coefficient absolute sum M

statement: Consider a finite simple graph with an FK(p,q) law, 0<p<1 and q>=1, with no imposed identification of vertices outside a chosen subgraph H. Suppose H has at least two distinct boundary vertices and boundary vertex v has k incident edges outside H. If xi is the partition of the boundary induced by open paths using only exterior edges, then P(xi is not the one-block wired partition)>=(1-p)^k. In a family of maximum degree D this is at least (1-p)^D>0. Therefore uniqueness of a giant component alone cannot justify an assertion that every fixed boundary vertex is wired together with probability tending to one.
assumptions: at least two distinct boundary vertices

statement: Let X,Y solve the synchronous Skorokhod equations in {|x|>=R}, R>0, with the same continuous driving path and inward-to-domain normal X/R or Y/R on the boundary. Write r=|X-Y| and let L_X,L_Y be their boundary regulators. Before r reaches zero, d log r = (1/(2R))(1-(|Y|^2-R^2)/r^2) dL_X + (1/(2R))(1-(|X|^2-R^2)/r^2) dL_Y. For reflected Brownian motions the same identity holds pathwise because the common Brownian increments cancel in X-Y. Thus coalescence at infinity is equivalent to this signed occupation functional tending to minus infinity. No sign or long-time behavior of that functional is proved here.
assumptions: normal reflection into the exterior domain
